title: Tailgating & Physical Badge Access Pretext

scenario.sender: Person with heavy delivery boxes outside corporate security doors
scenario.subject: Physical Security Access
scenario.body: You are swiping your employee badge to enter a secure corporate research facility. A person carrying two huge catering trays full of hot coffee and muffins rushes up behind you, smiling stressed: 'Hey! Could you please hold the door for a sec? My hands are totally full and my badge is in my backpack! Thanks so much!'
scenario.context: Simulated physical tailgating social engineering attack exploiting natural politeness.

options.text: COMPLY — Hold the door open politely because they are holding breakfast and look friendly
REFUSE POLITELY — Hold the door closed, explain security policy requires everyone to badge in independently, and direct them to the reception check-in desk
Take the donuts and let them inside

indicators.description: Classic physical penetration testing tactic exploiting social norms of politeness
Using props (coffee, heavy boxes, crutches) to prevent badge inspection
Bypasses electronic badge audit trail and physical access control

explanation: Tailgating (Piggybacking) relies on people's reluctance to seem rude or unhelpful. Physical red teamers and industrial spies regularly use props like coffee trays or fake delivery boxes to slip past badge readers without leaving an access log.
hints: Why is physical badge access individual and logged per person?
How do security auditors test employee compliance at entrance doors?
Polite security is firm security: 'I'm sorry, company policy requires all personnel and visitors to badge in or register at reception.'
learningObjective: Enforce strict physical access control and defeat tailgating pretexting without fear of social awkwardness.
consequenceChain: You held the door open for the pleasant individual carrying coffee
The individual was a corporate spy who placed a hardware packet sniffer (LAN Turtle) behind a conference room printer
Internal network traffic captured for 3 weeks undetected
recoverySteps: Escort unauthorized individual back to security reception desk immediately
Alert building physical security operations
Conduct floor sweep for planted rogue hardware implants

title: Authority Pretexting: Executive VIP Rush Request

scenario.sender: Executive VP of Product (via Direct Messaging)
scenario.subject: Urgent Board Meeting Deliverable
scenario.body: Hey, I'm currently presenting live in the board of directors room with the CEO. We need the unmasked customer dataset for our EMEA enterprise accounts exported to CSV immediately for our slide presentation. Don't submit an IT ticket — that takes 2 days. Upload it directly to my personal Dropbox right now. The CEO is watching the clock!
scenario.context: Authority pressure & fear-based social engineering bypassing compliance controls.

options.text: COMPLY — The VP and CEO need it immediately and you don't want to get fired
REJECT & VERIFY — Follow mandatory data governance protocol; never export unmasked PII to personal cloud storage or via informal chat
Email the data directly to all board members

indicators.description: Weaponizing executive hierarchy ('CEO is watching') to coerce rule violation
Explicit instruction to skip standard compliance/IT change control
Directing sensitive PII to personal unmanaged Dropbox account

explanation: Attackers pose as high-ranking executives to induce panic and intimidate employees into bypassing compliance safeguards. Legitimate executives understand that compliance and data protection rules cannot be overridden through informal chat requests.
hints: Why is the request pressuring you to bypass official data governance tickets?
Should sensitive customer PII ever be uploaded to personal cloud storage?
No executive request supersedes legal privacy regulations (GDPR/HIPAA).
learningObjective: Resist executive authority coercion and maintain data loss prevention protocols.
consequenceChain: You exported 100,000 customer records to the external Dropbox folder
The message was from an external attacker who compromised a secondary Slack token
Company suffered massive regulatory fine for willful data governance breach
recoverySteps: Notify Data Privacy Officer (DPO) and Legal Counsel
Rotate compromised data store credentials and audit database export logs
File breach notification with regulatory authorities within statutory timeframe

title: IT Helpdesk Caller ID Spoofing (Vishing)

scenario.subject: Incoming Phone Call
scenario.body: Your desk phone rings. Caller ID shows 'INTERNAL HELPDESK x100'. The caller says: 'Hi, this is Marcus from Tier 2 Network Ops. We're observing abnormal outbound DDoS traffic from your workstation IP. I need you to go to quick-support-remote.me so I can patch your network driver before security disables your switch port.'
scenario.context: Voice Phishing (Vishing) with spoofed internal Caller ID.

options.text: COMPLY — Caller ID clearly says 'INTERNAL HELPDESK' so it must be real IT
VERIFY OUT-OF-BAND — Hang up, check company internal directory, and call the verified IT desk extension directly to verify Marcus's ticket
Give him your Windows password over the phone instead

indicators.description: Caller ID numbers and text names can be easily spoofed using VoIP SIP trunks
Directs user to third-party unapproved remote control website
Threatens switch port disconnection to pressure immediate obedience

explanation: Caller ID is completely untrustworthy because VoIP phone technology allows anyone to display any phone number or name they want. Always hang up and call the published internal helpdesk number yourself.
hints: Can phone caller IDs be forged by external callers?
Why should you always hang up and initiate the call back yourself?
Does your real IT department use third-party '.me' websites for remote management?
learningObjective: Defeat Voice Phishing (Vishing) and recognize that Caller ID provides zero cryptographic proof of identity.
consequenceChain: You went to the website and ran the remote support executable
Vishing caller installed Cobalt Strike beacon on your endpoint
Attacker dumped LSASS memory and obtained domain administrator privileges
recoverySteps: Disconnect machine immediately from corporate Ethernet / Wi-Fi
Report active vishing attack to Security Operations Center
Re-image the compromised workstation from known-clean golden image

title: Baiting: Malicious USB Drive in Corporate Parking Lot

scenario.sender: Branded USB 3.0 Flash Drive found on asphalt near executive parking slot
scenario.subject: Physical Discovery
scenario.body: While walking into the office, you notice a sleek 128GB metallic USB flash drive on the ground labeled 'Q3 Executive Bonuses & Salary Benchmarks (Confidential)'. What should you do with it?
scenario.context: Simulated physical USB Drop / Baiting attack exploiting human curiosity.

options.text: Plug it into your work laptop to find the owner's resume or files so you can return it to them
Plug it into a friend's computer instead to be safe
DO NOT PLUG IT IN — Hand it directly to Corporate Physical Security / IT Security for safe isolation analysis

indicators.description: Classic physical baiting attack (Rubber Ducky / BadUSB / USB Killer)
Labeling device with enticing sensitive topics (salaries, executive plans)
Malicious USB microcontrollers emulate keyboards (HID) to inject keystroke exploits in milliseconds

explanation: Plugging an unknown USB drive into a computer is extremely dangerous. BadUSB hardware devices (such as USB Rubber Ducky or Bash Bunny) masquerade as keyboards, injecting hundreds of commands per second the instant they are inserted, bypassing antivirus.
hints: Can a USB flash drive contain a microcontroller that emulates a keyboard to hack your PC in 2 seconds?
Why are dropped USB drives strategically placed in executive parking lots?
Never insert unknown storage hardware into any computer.
learningObjective: Resist physical USB baiting attacks and understand BadUSB / HID keyboard injection vectors.
consequenceChain: You plugged the USB drive into your workstation
Device emulated a high-speed keyboard, opened PowerShell, and downloaded ransomware
All corporate network shares encrypted within 4 minutes
recoverySteps: Isolate affected network segments and restore systems from immutable backups
Enforce group policy (GPO) disabling USB removable storage on all corporate endpoints
Conduct physical sweep of campus grounds for additional dropped media

title: Watering Hole & Industry Forum Reconnaissance

scenario.sender: Private Message on Professional Developer Forum
scenario.subject: Help debugging custom cryptographic library
scenario.body: Hey! Saw your insightful post on StackOverflow regarding our mutual employer's internal microservices architecture. I'm building an open-source tool for engineers in our specific niche. Could you test this zero-dependency utility on your workstation and let me know if it solves the latency issue?
scenario.context: Watering hole / targeted developer supply chain reconnaissance attack (Lazarus style).

options.text: COMPLY — Run the benchmark script to help a fellow niche developer
ANALYZE & REFUSE — Review repo code in an isolated sandbox, never discuss internal company architecture online, and report the targeted outreach
Share your corporate GitHub API token with them

indicators.description: State-sponsored campaigns targeting software developers with malicious source repositories
Attacker mapped target's employment and technical stack via public social media and StackOverflow
Pre-compiled tar.gz containing malicious build script (postinstall hook)

explanation: Advanced threat groups (e.g. Lazarus/Diamond Sleet) create fake developer personas on LinkedIn, GitHub, and X. They flatter developers with collaboration requests or fake job interviews, then send trojanized coding tests that deploy malware upon execution.
hints: How did this stranger find information about your company's internal technology stack?
Why are developer workstations high-value targets for nation-state attackers?
Never execute unvetted third-party code on a corporate or personal development machine.
learningObjective: Identify targeted developer social engineering and avoid executing trojanized collaboration code.
consequenceChain: You ran npm install / tar.gz which executed an obfuscated post-install script
Malware stole SSH keys, AWS credentials, and source code repositories
Attacker pushed backdoor commit into company's main production branch
recoverySteps: Revoke and rotate all GitHub, AWS, and SSH signing keys
Audit git commit history and CI/CD pipelines for injected tampering
Review employee public social media profiles to eliminate internal architecture disclosures

title: The Desperate Job Applicant

scenario.subject: Please review my application - I really need this job!
scenario.body: Hi, I saw you work at this company. I am desperate for a job to support my family. Please look at my resume (attached) and put in a good word for me? I even wrote a cover letter specifically for you.

options.text: COMPLY — Open the document out of pity to help them out
REJECT — Do not open unsolicited attachments, refer them to the official careers portal
Forward to the CEO directly

indicators.description: Using pity to bypass security logic
Malicious payload delivery via resume lure

explanation: Attackers use emotional triggers (pity, fear, greed) to force you into making a mistake, like opening a macro-enabled Word document.
hints: Why would they bypass the normal career portal?
Can a Word document contain malware?
learningObjective: Never open unsolicited attachments regardless of the emotional story attached.
consequenceChain: You opened the Word document
Macro virus executed
Ransomware deployed across the network
recoverySteps: Isolate the machine
Run anti-virus scans
Report the phishing attempt

title: Fake LinkedIn Recruiter

scenario.subject: Incredible 300k/yr Opportunity
scenario.body: Hi there! Your profile is amazing. I have an unlisted VP role at a Fortune 500 paying  base. I need your updated resume with your full home address and personal phone number to submit you for the interview today.
scenario.context: Greed-based OSINT gathering via fake recruiter profiles.

options.text: COMPLY — Give them your personal details, 300k is a lot of money!
REJECT & VERIFY — Check their profile age, connections, and refuse to give PII upfront
Give them your corporate credit card

indicators.description: Offering unrealistic salaries to bypass critical thinking

explanation: Fake recruiters are used by threat actors to map corporate structures, harvest personal data for spear-phishing, or build a rapport before sending malicious coding tests.
hints: Does a legitimate recruiter demand a home address immediately?
Is a  salary offer out of nowhere realistic?
learningObjective: Identify and ignore greed-based social engineering on professional networks.
consequenceChain: You gave your details
Your identity was stolen
Your accounts were compromised via SIM swapping
recoverySteps: Block the recruiter
Report the profile to LinkedIn
Enable MFA on all accounts
